core_obligations: Assume the kernel inclusion holds after tensoring with every finitely presented module Q (proof lines 21141-21142).
For an arbitrary module Q, write it as a directed colimit of finitely presented modules Q_i and note that the inclusion holds for each Q_i (proof lines 21143-21147).
Use that directed colimits are exact and commute with tensor products to conclude the inclusion for Q itself, giving domination (proof lines 21147-21149).
proof_roadmap: Reduce an arbitrary test module to a directed colimit of finitely presented ones (proof lines 21140-21145).
Transport the kernel inclusion through the exact functor given by tensoring and taking the colimit (proof lines 21145-21150).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that one module map dominates another exactly when the kernel inclusions hold after tensoring with every finitely presented module (statement lines 21132-21138). The proof does not rework the definition of domination: it assumes the inclusions for finitely presented modules, writes an arbitrary module as a directed colimit of finitely presented ones, and then uses exactness of the directed colimit together with its commutation with the tensor product to pass the inclusion to the colimit (proof lines 21140-21150). The two categorical properties invoked, exactness and commutation with tensor products, are the whole content, and the author names both. H2.
